vectors.description: Keywords are case-insensitive and print in upper case
A # comment runs to the end of the line; \r\n is a line break
Names keep their case
Any text between backticks is a name, keywords included
In single quotes a quote is written twice and nothing else is escaped
Double-quoted strings have the escapes of JSON
Digits are an int, a fraction makes an exact decimal with its scale, an exponent a float

given.rules_text: a = 42 AND b = 2.50 AND c = 1.5e0 AND d = 1E-7 AND e = 2e+3

expect.printed: a = 42 AND b = 2.50 AND c = 1.5e0 AND d = 1e-7 AND e = 2000e0

vectors.description: A float prints with its shortest digits: plain with e0 when its magnitude is within [1e-4, 1e16), with an exponent otherwise
A minus directly before a number makes a negative constant
A minus not directly before a number negates; it prints with parentheses
DATE, DATETIME, DECIMAL and FLOAT take the text of the typed forms

given.rules_text: d = DATE "2026-10-31" AND t > DATETIME "2026-10-31T09:30:00+01:00" AND e = DECIMAL "5" AND g = FLOAT "-inf" AND h = float "1.5"

expect.printed: d = DATE "2026-10-31" AND t > DATETIME "2026-10-31T09:30:00+01:00" AND e = DECIMAL "5" AND g = FLOAT "-inf" AND h = 1.5e0

vectors.description: An unquoted 2026-10-31 is a subtraction, never a date
TRUE and FALSE are constants; == and <> are = and !=
A boolean constant stands alone as a condition
AND binds tighter than OR
Parentheses that change the tree are printed
Parentheses that do not change the tree are not printed
A chain of AND is one node, and so is a parenthesized one inside it

given.rules_text: a AND b AND (c AND d) OR (e OR f)

expect.printed: a AND b AND c AND d OR e OR f

vectors.description: &, | and ~ are AND, OR and NOT, as in fuzzytool

expect.printed: a AND b OR NOT c

vectors.description: NOT before a predicate needs no parentheses

given.rules_text: NOT x > 5 AND NOT (a OR b)

expect.printed: NOT x > 5 AND NOT (a OR b)

vectors.description: IN lists constants
x NOT IN (...) is NOT of IN, and prints that way
The AND of BETWEEN belongs to it; CLOSED is both when omitted

given.rules_text: x BETWEEN 1 AND 10 AND y BETWEEN a + 1 AND b CLOSED left

expect.printed: x BETWEEN 1 AND 10 AND y BETWEEN a + 1 AND b CLOSED LEFT

vectors.description: x NOT BETWEEN is NOT of BETWEEN

given.rules_text: x NOT BETWEEN 0 AND 1 CLOSED NONE

expect.printed: NOT x BETWEEN 0 AND 1 CLOSED NONE

vectors.description: IS NULL and IS NOT NULL

given.rules_text: a IS NULL OR b IS NOT NULL

expect.printed: a IS NULL OR NOT b IS NULL

vectors.description: MATCHES, STARTS WITH, ENDS WITH and CONTAINS, each with NOT

given.rules_text: s MATCHES '^a.*' AND s STARTS WITH "ab" AND s NOT ENDS WITH 'z' AND s not contains "q"

expect.printed: s MATCHES "^a.*" AND s STARTS WITH "ab" AND NOT s ENDS WITH "z" AND NOT s CONTAINS "q"

vectors.description: * and / bind tighter than + and -, which are left-associative

given.rules_text: a + b * c - d / e > (a + b) * c - (d - e)

expect.printed: a + b * c - d / e > (a + b) * c - (d - e)

vectors.description: Unary minus binds tightest; ABS takes a value
Paths have .name and [index] segments, and may start with an index
Either side of a comparison may be a constant or a field
A parenthesized node starts at its parenthesis
A rule with a RULE header

given.rules_text:
RULE vip PRIORITY 10
IF customer.years > 5 AND order.total > 1000
THEN discount = 0.15

expect.printed:
RULE vip PRIORITY 10
IF customer.years > 5 AND order.total > 1000
THEN discount = 0.15

vectors.description: Without a RULE header, a rule is named rule_<n>

expect.printed:
RULE rule_1
IF a > 1
THEN x = 1

vectors.description: The payload is optional
Names and tags are names or strings; payload values are any expression

given.rules_text:
RULE "big order" PRIORITY -3 TAGS gold, 'two words' DESCRIPTION "for big orders"
IF total > 1000
THEN discount = 0.10, 'unit price' = total * 0.21

expect.printed:
RULE "big order" PRIORITY -3 TAGS gold, "two words" DESCRIPTION "for big orders"
IF total > 1000
THEN discount = 0.10, "unit price" = total * 0.21

vectors.description: A payload value is a value, not a condition; the error is at the value

given.rules_text:
RULE r IF a
THEN late = days > 30

vectors.description: A rule set with a header

given.rules_text:
HIT POLICY priority

RULE vip PRIORITY 10 TAGS gold, loyalty
IF customer.years > 5 AND order.total > 1000
THEN discount = 0.15, label = "VIP"

RULE loyal PRIORITY 5
IF customer.years > 2 OR customer.newsletter
THEN discount = 0.05

expect.printed:
HIT POLICY priority

RULE vip PRIORITY 10 TAGS gold, loyalty
IF customer.years > 5 AND order.total > 1000
THEN discount = 0.15, label = "VIP"

RULE loyal PRIORITY 5
IF customer.years > 2 OR customer.newsletter
THEN discount = 0.05

vectors.description: Several rules without a header are a rule set with the first hit policy

given.rules_text:
IF a THEN x = 1
IF b THEN x = 2

expect.printed:
HIT POLICY first

RULE rule_1
IF a
THEN x = 1

RULE rule_2
IF b
THEN x = 2

vectors.description: AGGREGATE, LOGIC and STRICT header lines; LOGIC boolean is not printed

given.rules_text:
hit policy COLLECT
aggregate sum
logic boolean
strict
RULE r IF a > 1 THEN x = 1

expect.printed:
HIT POLICY collect
AGGREGATE sum
STRICT

RULE r
IF a > 1
THEN x = 1

vectors.description: One rule after a header is a rule set

expect.printed:
HIT POLICY unique

RULE rule_1
IF a

vectors.description: A predicate has one comparison at most
An unexpected end is located one past the last character
An unclosed string is located at its quote
An unclosed backtick name is located at its backtick
A double-quoted string has only the escapes of JSON
A character outside the syntax
IN lists constants only
Lines and columns count \r\n as one line break

given.rules_text:
RULE r
IF x >
THEN y = 1

vectors.description: After a dot any identifier is a key, keywords included, as written
A key after a dot is an identifier or a name between backticks
A rule needs IF
A condition is the whole text
An unknown hit policy is a syntax error at its name
An unknown logic is a registry error at its name
A float literal beyond the float range
An int literal beyond 64 bits
The smallest int is a negative constant
An index is a non-negative integer
A typed literal's text is checked like its typed form
A construction error is located where its node starts
IN values of different type groups
A text that is a value is not a condition
A rule set error is located at the rule it names

given.rules_text:
RULE a IF x
RULE a IF y

vectors.description: Texts have the size limit of documents
The depth limit stops at the first node completed that goes deeper
Payload values have the depth limit too
A chain of arithmetic nests to the left and has the depth limit
Parentheses, NOT, - and ABS nest at most 2 x max_depth + 2 deep
Parentheses within the nesting limit are read
A payload key written twice is located at its second occurrence

given.rules_text: RULE r IF a THEN x = 1, x = 2

vectors.description: A number does not start with 0 followed by digits, as in JSON
Strings between single quotes hold no control characters
Whitespace is spaces, tabs and line breaks only
A byte order mark may start the text
The text of a typed literal is exactly its form
Header lines come in their order

given.rules_text: STRICT HIT POLICY first IF a

vectors.description: A condition exactly at the depth limit is read
Floats print with the shortest digits that read back, and FLOAT "…" when infinite

expect.printed: a = 1e0 AND b = 0.1e0 AND c = 123456.789e0 AND d = FLOAT "inf"

vectors.description: Decimals print with their scale, DECIMAL when the scale is 0

expect.printed: a = DECIMAL "5" AND b = -1.500 AND c = DECIMAL "inf"

vectors.description: The negation of a number constant prints with parentheses
Keys that are not names print between backticks, other labels as strings

expect.printed:
RULE "if" TAGS "a-b", c
IF `if`.`a b`.x = 1
THEN "unit price" = 1, ok = 2

vectors.description: Nested and and or are flattened; arithmetic keeps its parentheses

expect.printed: (a OR b OR c) AND d AND e AND x - (y + z) > p / (q * r)

vectors.description: Strings print with JSON escapes; NULL is a constant
A rule with metadata has no text
A field key with a control character has no text
A rule set always prints its hit policy

expect.printed:
HIT POLICY first

RULE r
IF a

vectors.description: DO names the rule's action, on its own line

given.rules_text: RULE vip IF a > 1 THEN x = 1 DO notify

expect.printed:
RULE vip
IF a > 1
THEN x = 1
DO notify

vectors.description: DO without a payload, in a rule without a header

expect.printed:
RULE rule_1
IF a > 1
DO notify

vectors.description: An action name that is not a name is a string
Each rule names its own action

given.rules_text:
HIT POLICY rule_order
RULE a IF a > 1 DO notify
RULE b IF a > 1 THEN x = 1
RULE c IF a > 1 DO notify

expect.printed:
HIT POLICY rule_order

RULE a
IF a > 1
DO notify

RULE b
IF a > 1
THEN x = 1

RULE c
IF a > 1
DO notify

vectors.description: DO is a keyword: a field named do is written between backticks
A bare do is the keyword
An empty action name, located at the string
DO needs a name
A rule names one action

given.rules_text: IF a > 1 DO a DO b

vectors.description: DO comes after THEN

given.rules_text: IF a > 1 DO a THEN x = 1
